features.name: v1_v2_ratio
features.description: Ratio of V1 to the absolute value of V2 (plus a constant to avoid division by zero), capturing the relative magnitude of these two primary features.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a normalized ratio of two primary heuristic features, allowing the linear SVM to capture their relative magnitude without instability near zero.

features.name: v12_v28_max
features.description: The maximum value between V12 and V28, which are both features with potentially large positive outliers.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the extreme values of two high-variance features, providing a strong margin signal for cases where either heuristic spikes.

features.name: v9_v13_v15_composite
features.description: A simple linear sum of V9, V13, and V15, aggregating features that share similar high-magnitude distributions.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a linear composite of related high-magnitude features, reducing dimensionality and providing a smoother signal for the SVM margin.

features.name: v45_v51_min
features.description: The minimum value between V45 and V51, capturing the lower bound of two features with negative skew.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the lower bound of two negatively skewed features, useful for defining a decision boundary based on minimum threshold conditions.

features.name: v1_to_v5_l2_approx
features.description: Approximate L2 norm of the first five features, representing their combined magnitude in a Euclidean space.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a continuous severity measure of the first five features' combined magnitude, transforming a spherical region into a linear feature for the SVM.

features.name: v12_log_transform
features.description: Logarithmic transformation of V12 to compress its long positive tail.
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses the long tail of V12, preventing extreme outliers from dominating the linear SVM weights and improving margin stability.

features.name: v28_v29_diff
features.description: The linear difference between V28 and V29, measuring their divergence.
features.expected_model_benefit: Explicitly provides the linear difference between two highly variable features, allowing the SVM to directly weight their divergence.

features.name: v33_v43_interaction
features.description: Multiplicative interaction between V33 and V43, which both have relatively low variance.
features.expected_model_benefit: Introduces a multiplicative interaction between two low-variance features, enabling the linear model to capture their combined effect.

features.name: high_value_count_approx
features.description: Counts the number of features among a selected subset (V9, V12, V13, V15, V21, V22, V28, V29) that exceed a threshold of 5.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a discrete count of extreme heuristic values, acting as a step-function severity measure that can strongly influence the SVM decision boundary.
features.formula: np.where(V9>5,1,0) + np.where(V12>5,1,0) + np.where(V13>5,1,0) + np.where(V15>5,1,0) + np.where(V21>5,1,0) + np.where(V22>5,1,0) + np.where(V28>5,1,0) + np.where(V29>5,1,0)

features.name: v1_v2_v3_v4_v5_mean
features.description: The arithmetic mean of the first five features.
features.expected_model_benefit: Averages the first five features to create a low-variance, smooth composite score, ideal for stable linear SVM weight assignment.

features.name: heuristic_complexity_judgment
features.description: Semantic assessment of the overall complexity of the theorem proving state, based on the magnitude and distribution of search-related variables.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a holistic, continuous severity measure of complexity that may not be easily captured by simple linear combinations, aiding in margin separation.

features.name: proof_search_stability_judgment
features.description: Semantic assessment of the stability of the proof search, evaluating the variance and presence of extreme values across the heuristic features.
features.expected_model_benefit: Offers a normalized score representing search stability, allowing the linear SVM to adjust its confidence or decision boundary based on state volatility.
